A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the degraded stiffness is a key factor for the strain localization in shear band, the second-order shear strain gradients are not necessary for the stability of the localized shear band.
the degraded stiffness is important for the deformation behavior of shear band and it is reasonable to consider the degraded stiffness in the constitutive relation of shear band.
the degraded stiffness in the present model can be used to describe the strain-softenning phenomenon and the gradient-dependent plasticity can be used to explain the strain localization in rock.
The main takeaway from our work is that

degraded stiffness should be considered in the strain softening process of shear band, and the second-order shear strain gradients should be introduced in the context of the classical plasticity theory.
the degraded stiffness should not be neglected in the strain-weakening process.
the degraded stiffness in strain-softening shear band can be taken into consideration by the gradient-dependent plasticity theory.
